newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken completes debt offering.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken completes debt offering.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc said Monday it completed an offering of $287.5 million in debt early in the second quarter.

"Early in the second quarter, we completed an offering of $287.5 million in convertible subordinated debentures, despite what we consider to be the most volatile and difficult market conditions we've faced since going public in November 1993." said Mark Stephens, vice chairman and chief financial officer.
Boston Chicken today reported first quarter net income increased 37 percent, to $21.4 million from $15.6 million a year earlier.

Earnings per share increased 33 percent, to $0.32 from $0.24, while revenues rose 147 percent to $116.8 million from $47.34 million, reflecting an increase in revenue from company stores, due primarily to a higher average number of such stores in 1997.
Earnings per share were in line with the Zacks estimate. Zacks sees the company earning $0.33 per share in the second quarter and $1.37 for the full year.

"The first quarter was marked by several significant events," said Scott Beck, chairman, chief executive officer and president. "We increased our company store base through the 118-store conversion of BC New York, which is already having a positive contribution to earnings; we completed installation of our Boston Carver line with the introduction of Extreme Carver sandwiches; and we began to explore the potential for Boston Market branded, ready-to-heat meals."
Boston Chicken said its majority-owned subsidiary Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp is "rapidly becoming the leading specialty bagel retailer in the U.S."
